This study investigates the discretization of a distributed regulation mechanism targeting the stochastic evolution of a first-order hyperbolic system. The specific distributed feedback is engineered such that the corresponding deterministic variant is exactly solvable via separation of variables. To analyze system stability, a discrete transformation is employed to transform the stochastic partial differential equation into an ordinary one through the use of an integral operator. The primary outcomes establish both the necessary and sufficient conditions for mean square exponential stability and the conditions ensuring almost sure exponential stability. Additionally, it is demonstrated that if the spatial discretization is sufficiently fine, the stability of the discrete system is guaranteed.

This study examines cosmic rays with energies exceeding 4 EeV detected at the Pierre Auger Observatory, focusing on fluctuations in the arrival rates of particles within specific solid-angle regions centered on the sky distribution. The analysis covers a 10-year timeframe from 2004 to 2014, revealing that the resulting angular distribution of these rate variations conforms to a Gaussian distribution with a width of approximately 15\% and exhibits no significant drift over the study duration. The research further explores potential origins for these large-scale fluctuations, including the influence of the source distribution, the impact of the Earth's magnetic field, and the influence of interstellar turbulence.

This structure was originally introduced by O. Chein in 1966 within the context of commutative right zeros semigroups. The current paper establishes that any zinbiel algebra satisfying a nontrivial identity must be abelian. Furthermore, the study fully characterizes the form of these algebras when the identity is specifically commutativity.

Employing the method of flow intensity and fluctuations in the stream angle alongside correlations with the stream angle, we investigate the connection between these variations and initial-state irregularities. The observed stream angle fluctuations are found to be approximately 0.002, with corresponding intensity fluctuations of roughly 0.002, which aligns with hydrodynamic model predictions. These results indicate that the initial state exhibits significant spatial anisotropy, a key driver for the generation of initial transverse flow intensity fluctuations.

This paper examines the problem of reconciling inconsistent tables that contain missing values and functional dependencies. We introduce a specific class of fillers, referred to as "k-tuple fillers," which are capable of generating at most $k$ copies for any null value. We demonstrate that identifying a 2-tuple filler is NP-complete, whereas determining a 3-tuple filler remains an open question. Furthermore, we establish polynomial-time algorithms to decide the existence of a tuple filler for tables without dependencies or with acyclic dependencies.

This paper introduces the TVPAR model, designed to simultaneously model and forecast the multiple interrelated Poisson time series. The TVPAR framework consists of three main elements: first, it employs an orthogonal Temporal-Varying Poisson Regression (TVPR) model to define the conditional mean of each series based on the entire history of all series; second, the coefficients linking current and past values are constrained to form temporal autocorrelation structures that vary over time; and finally, current counts are allowed to have a direct impact on the mean of all series. We propose an efficient estimation approach for these models and demonstrate through both simulation studies and real-world data that TVPAR achieves superior forecasting accuracy compared to existing methods.

We introduce Neural Descriptor Fields (NDFs) as a novel object representation designed to enhance robotic grasping. An object's pose relative to the camera is determined by matching its novel 6D description to a database entry, enabling the system to localize objects even without an explicit 3D model. Because these fields are SE(3)-invariant, they possess strong discriminative capabilities and can efficiently be stored. Experiments show that these field-based descriptions outperform current state-of-the-art methods in both real-world and simulated scenarios for object localization. Furthermore, we utilize these field-based descriptions to execute view-dependent grasp execution trajectories that dynamically adjust based on the object's actual pose in space.

This study introduces a novel technique for monitoring aerosol optical depth (AOD) by utilizing stellar photometry. This method offers continuous monitoring capabilities and high temporal resolution, effectively bridging gaps left by satellite and coarsely monitored AOD data. The approach was tested on the V and B photometry of 2000 stars, collected over a decade via the 2.3-meter telescope at the Kiso Observatory. The resulting 10-day-long time series for each star was used to calculate an individualized, location-specific conversion factor linking photometric variations to changes in the vertical AOD at the star's zenith distance. The study demonstrates that this method achieves a sensitivity of approximately 0.01 units per star, corresponding to a zenith AOD change of roughly 0.01. The derived factor exhibits strong stability over time, with a standard uncertainty of 0.03 units/p factor/p star/p over the observation period. The resulting per-star time-averaged AOD maps were generated using data from three sites: Kiso, Japan; La Silla, Chile; and Mauna Kea, Hawaii. Results indicate that this method can map spatial variations in the mean AOD with a resolution of approximately 100 km. The paper concludes by outlining potential applications of this method for various research domains.

Full 6DoF pose estimation represents a critical capability for robotic systems, yet it remains challenging due to the inherent noise in visual correspondence and the inherent redundancy within projection groups. This study introduces an innovative framework that leverages both correspondence learning and projection grouping to enhance pose estimation performance. We present a novel method for integrating projections that accounts for varying noise levels, thereby optimizing the likelihood function. Furthermore, we develop a deep learning model designed to predict visual correspondences directly in image space. Extensive evaluations conducted on both public datasets and real-world robotic scenarios demonstrate the method's superior accuracy and robustness across diverse applications.

We introduce GGLasso, a Python library designed to solve Generalized Graphical Lasso computations. This method estimates the precision matrix for a multivariate distribution by maximizing its log-likelihood subject to a constraint on the graph's edge weights. We highlight several advantages of this approach, including its applicability to multivariate distributions without requiring assumptions about their structure, the ability to estimate correlations among large datasets via parallel processing, and the capacity to recover multiple structures simultaneously across various distributions. We demonstrate GGLasso's utility in estimating the structure of multiple gene regulatory networks and provide the associated code on GitHub at https://github.com/yourname/GGLasso.

Configurational sampling constitutes a fundamental challenge in molecular dynamics simulations, with the efficacy of existing methods heavily dependent on the specific algorithm employed for estimating numerical integrals. This study introduces a self-correcting configurational sampling methodology that leverages the Langevin dynamics framework combined with the Monte Carlo Metropolis-Hastings algorithm to estimate these integrals. The proposed technique guarantees exact convergence to the canonical ensemble without requiring an infinitesimal time step, offering superior efficiency compared to standard Molecular Dynamics protocols. Additionally, the approach delivers precise temperature control, ensuring adherence to the target canonical distribution. The utility and precision of this method are validated through two distinct case studies: a simple harmonic oscillator and a liquid argon model.

The concept of eigenvector centrality has long been utilized to assess the importance of nodes within a graph, under the assumption that a node gains significance through its connections to other highly important nodes. However, this traditional approach often falls short when applied to multilayer networks, as it typically treats each layer's node importance independently and fails to account for cross-layer dependencies. This study introduces a refined framework for eigenvector prominence in multilayer networks that explicitly addresses two critical shortcomings: first, it ensures the independence of importance metrics across different types of reliance, and second, it incorporates the significance of nodes that exist and interact across multiple layers simultaneously. To achieve this, we propose a general mathematical model for reliant node importance capable of representing various dependency structures among nodes. Furthermore, we define the prominence of nodes in multilayer systems by synthesizing their individual layer-based importance scores with the importance derived from their roles as connectors between layers. We provide explicit calculations for prominence under specific reliance scenarios, including orthogonal and uniform models. Finally, we validate our approach through numerical simulations and an empirical analysis of a real-world multilayer air transportation network.

This paper presents a novel interpretation of R-minkowski spacetime, offering an alternative formulation of the Dirac equation within this framework that aligns perfectly with the standard version in ordinary Minkowski spacetime. We demonstrate that the previously introduced "duality" between the conventional gamma matrices and the R-matrix representation constitutes an isomorphism, effectively treating the R-matrix not merely as a computational tool but as a genuine, independent entity. Furthermore, we establish a commutative, associative, and non-divisible ring structure for the R-matrix elements, proving via an explicit construction that the R-gamma matrices form a genuine Clifford algebra. Additionally, we define a new concept termed the "R-spinor," which possesses twice the degree compared to a standard spinor. Finally, we verify through explicit calculation that the reinterpreted R-matrix Dirac equation satisfies all essential properties of its original counterpart.

This study investigates the surface-sealed liquid droplets formed when a wetted sphere impacts an opposing fluid pool. The analysis covers a range of Stefen numbers from 0.02 to 0.2 and impact velocities between 0.1 and 2.0 m/s. The relationship is examined linking the minimum pool surface depression to the Stefen number, supported by high-resolution imaging techniques capturing both the depression dynamics and the surface tension gradient. The observed surface tension gradient is attributed to variations in the depth of the v-shaped wedge located at the sphere-pool interface. The findings indicate that the depth of the surface depression increases with both impact speed and Stefen number. Furthermore, the study reveals a distinct transition regime characterized by a change in the surface tension gradient mechanism as the Stefen number increases. These results are relevant to understanding similar phenomena in contexts such as internal combustion engine fuel injection.

A persistent open problem in string theory concerns the mechanism by which continuous global symmetries are broken. We examine this issue within the context of Type IIB $\mathcal{N}=2$ supergravity effective field theories (EFTs) augmented by coupled axions and moduli. Our findings demonstrate that the cancellation of an anomalous extended theta-term—anomaly being protected by a generalized global anomaly—necessitates the inclusion of a quantum-corrected theta-term. Crucily, this new term relies on a function of the coupled axions and moduli. Consequently, the generalized global anomaly ensures the theory's consistency only when these functions maintain a specific periodicity. We establish that such periodicity is guaranteed precisely when the theory preserves a certain $SL(2,\mathbb{Z})$ duality symmetry in the classical limit. Furthermore, we illustrate how this symmetry can be spontaneously broken via a vacuum expectation value for an uncharged scalar field, thereby breaking the associated continuous global symmetry.

The superconducting phase observed in Cu-doped CuFe2S3 (Tc = 28 K) has drawn significant attention due to theories suggesting it results from the formation of a non-magnetic singlet between the Cu 3d and Fe 3d orbitals. However, the orbital-selective nature of these states remains unclear. This study employs high-resolution ARPES and DFT calculations to reveal that the cupric ion exists as Cu2+ with a filled 3d9 configuration. Consequently, the electronic bands near the Fermi level are derived from Cu2+ ions, exhibiting a narrow bandwidth and strong correlation effects, whereas the Fe ions contribute broader bands with lower correlation strength. These findings indicate an orbital-selective Mott insulating phase where Cu orbitals become insulating while Fe orbitals remain metallic. Ultimately, this work demonstrates that the magnetic ordering in Cu1-xFe2S3 originates from the Fe sublattice, while the driving force for the subsequent superconductivity is attributed to the Cu orbitals.

Rabi oscillations represent a fundamental light-matter interaction phenomenon, yet achieving significantly large Rabi frequencies typically requires either strong external magnetic fields or the use of excitons. This study demonstrates that excitons can exhibit Rabi oscillations reaching approximately 10 meV—roughly five times the full width at half maximum of the spectral line—even in the complete absence of external magnetic fields. This enhancement stems from the combination of strong light-matter coupling and screening effects inherent to excitons. Crucially, this "hidden" Rabi oscillation regime, where oscillation amplitudes exceed line broadening, remains undetectable in standard absorption measurements. Nevertheless, it can be successfully revealed and characterized using circular dichroism techniques.

The two-dimensional (2D) honeycomb lattice, known for its Dirac points where conduction and valence bands touch, has garnered significant interest. Although various types of 2D honeycomb structures have been investigated, achieving tunable Dirac points remains challenging. In this study, we propose a 2D non-symmorphic wallpaper lattice featuring tunable Dirac points. We demonstrate that the non-symmorphic nature of the lattice, combined with specific on-site and hopping parameters, enables the adjustment of the touching point's position and the alteration of the touching geometry from linear to parabolic. Furthermore, we find that introducing spin-orbit coupling induces a gap opening at these points. Given the spin-locked nature of the currents generated by these lattices, we suggest their potential application in designing high-efficiency, low-power spintronic devices.

Coherent states, which are superpositions of distinct Fock states, are fundamental to quantum optics and underpin many cutting-edge technologies. However, creating single-photon facilitated coherent states—superpositions involving a fixed single photon and varying vacuum states—has remained challenging due to the inherent difficulty in generating on-the-fly single photons. This paper proposes a solution using optical catalysis to produce these states via a catalytic interaction between an incident probe field and an initially present single photon. We demonstrate that when the probe is strongly coupled to the catalyst, the combined system evolves into a separable state between the catalyst and probe. Consequently, the probe emerges in a single-photon facilitated coherent state, while the catalyst returns to its vacuum state. Furthermore, we analyze the non-classical properties of the generated single-photon facilitated coherent states.

This paper introduces a novel method for generating molecular structures from specific properties, addressing the widespread challenge of creating molecules with desired characteristics. The proposed algorithm utilizes linear regression to establish a mapping between molecular fingerprints and a target property, followed by integer linear programming to ensure the resulting structures adhere to valid chemical principles. We evaluated this approach on three distinct datasets: the Augis et al. collection for pKa values, the GOMEZA database for solubility (LogS), and the OpenOCL database for oxygen combustion energy (Hc). Results demonstrate the method's success in predicting the reported properties of test sets and effectively identifying molecules with similar characteristics within open molecular libraries.

Diseases affecting the esophagus, such as cancer and inflammation, pose significant threats to human health. Early detection and precise diagnosis are essential for effective treatment and improved patient outcomes. While radiologists currently rely on manual segmentation of neoplasms in CT scans to detect these conditions, this approach is labor-intensive, time-consuming, and prone to variability. Although existing deep learning models have demonstrated strong performance in medical image analysis, their application to esophageal tumor segmentation often struggles with small, irregular tumors obscured by surrounding tissue noise. To overcome these challenges, this study proposes the Diluted Dense Attention Unet (DDAUnet) architecture. This model integrates dilated convolution to expand the receptive field without increasing computational costs and incorporates dense connections to facilitate efficient information flow. Furthermore, two distinct attention mechanisms are employed to automatically emphasize tumor regions while suppressing irrelevant background interference. The DDAUnet was evaluated on 100 CT scans containing esophageal neoplasms, which were segmented by radiologists. The proposed architecture achieved a Dice Similarity Coefficient (DSC) of 0.811, a sensitivity of 0.881, and a mean Hausdorff Distance (MHD) of 10.11 pixels. These results indicate that DDAUnet delivers high-precision segmentation of esophageal neoplasms, making it a valuable tool to assist radiologists in early and accurate diagnosis.

Automatic image description models are typically evaluated using reference-free metrics, as most current evaluation datasets lack human-generated references. However, these metrics often yield lower correlations with human judgments compared to reference-dependent metrics. To bridge this gap, we propose a new approach that leverages minimal reference information from a single human annotator for a specific image to construct descriptions by automatic models. This method involves training an encoder-decoder translator using a small dataset of 2000 image-description pairs, where the description sentences are adapted to match the textual reference derived from the target annotator's image-specific commentary. Our analysis indicates that descriptions generated via this adaptation technique significantly enhance the performance of reference-free evaluation metrics.

Tantalum oxide (Ta$_2$O$_5$) is a dielectric material that has attracted significant interest for its potential in next-generation gate dielectrics and ferroelectric applications. However, the lack of a well-defined crystal structure model for this substance has hindered the accurate simulation of its properties. This study addresses this gap by employing advanced crystal structure prediction techniques, specifically the Total Energy Monte Carlo (TEMC) method and molecular dynamics simulations utilizing the Vienna Ab-initio Simulation Package (VASP). These approaches were implemented to identify the most thermodynamically stable structure and the corresponding interatomic potentials for Ta$_2$O$_5$. The results indicate that the base state of this material is an orthorhombic structure, designated as $\beta$-Ta$_2$O$_5$, which aligns with existing experimental data. Furthermore, the research reveals a strong correlation between the structural stability of the material and the oxidation states of its constituent atoms.

This study examines the role of Reddit's initial geographic sorting feature, introduced in 2015, which ordered posts by the user's proximity to the observer. Despite the platform's global user base, this sorting method was rarely utilized. We posit that its scarcity stems from the fact that, for many subreddits, the most harmful misinformation was disseminated through geographically distant posts, rendering the tool ineffective at curbing such content. Supporting this hypothesis, our analysis reveals that the top 100 most upvoted posts within 100 randomly selected subreddits contained false information in 20 instances. Furthermore, 18 of these 20 posts claimed to originate from a location geographically distant from the viewer, indicating that the sorting feature failed to address the primary channels of misinformation distribution. We conclude by proposing future enhancements to the geographic sorting mechanism designed to more efficiently combat online falsehoods.

Human-robot collaboration is increasingly vital, yet it faces challenges due to the complex communication required between species. While robots can learn manipulation tasks from demonstrations, current methods primarily rely on video data, often neglecting audio. This study investigates audio patterns in human instructors demonstrating tasks to robots. We analyze the acoustic characteristics of these instructors and compare them against synthetic speech patterns. Our findings reveal that Instructor speech exhibits distinct, non-random acoustic features compared to generated speech. These results indicate a clear need for future research into these patterns, as incorporating an understanding of human instructional audio could significantly enhance the effectiveness of robots learning manipulation skills.

The paper demonstrates that the intracacy—a complexity measure rooted in geometric and analytic properties of conformal mapping functions—evolves according to the Euler-Arnold equations defined on the Lie algebra of vector fields with growth conditions. This dynamic evolution of CFT complexity mirrors the behavior of complexity in quantum computational circuits.

We introduce the Talkbench framework, designed to facilitate the creation of automated tests for conversational systems. The framework operates by defining scenarios composed of user input sequences and corresponding expected system outputs, which are then executed to validate adherence to specified behaviors. We leverage data from real-world chat applications to build these tests, uncovering previously unknown bugs and validating their efficacy through deployment in production. To assess broader utility, we applied Talkbench to two chat-based systems: a customer support assistant and a popular chat application plugin, successfully identifying and resolving multiple bugs. Furthermore, we analyzed the framework's applicability to domain adaptation, concluding that Talkbench can be readily extended to test other conversational systems.

Recommendation systems are increasingly facing the challenge of sparsity, which hampers their ability to provide accurate suggestions. To overcome this limitation, this paper introduces a Multi-Sparse-Domain Cooperative Recommendation (MSCR) framework designed to leverage information from diverse domains. The core of MSCR is an enhanced comprehensive attribute preference learning (CAPL) module that integrates both explicit and implicit user attributes to deliver a more holistic view of user preferences. Furthermore, the proposed domain cooperation mechanism (DCM) facilitates the exchange of information across sparse domains by identifying commonalities among users within each domain and projecting these similarities into shared embedding spaces. This ensures that data scarcity in one domain does not impede performance in others. Extensive experiments conducted on five real-world datasets demonstrate that MSCR significantly outperforms existing baseline methods.

This paper introduces Hypatia. jl, an open-source package written in Julia designed to solve mathematical problems by representing variables and conic constraints using specialized "natural" forms. The tool aims to enhance the readability, efficiency, and robustness of code within optimization workflows. Hypatia. jl currently supports formulations for second-order cones, positive semidefinite cones, exponential cones, and rotated second-order cones. The article demonstrates the benefits of this library through practical examples, including a portfolio optimization model built with first-order cone representations and a stochastic dual dynamic programming (SDDP) reservoir management model based on an inverse hydrologic problem. Additionally, Hypatia. jl integrates seamlessly with Gurobi. jl and the JuMP modeling framework, while its future roadmap envisions support for additional cone types and third-party packages.

High-quality data is fundamental to the success of brain MRI research. Although automated quality assurance (QMQA) tools have been created to detect poor image quality, these systems frequently struggle when deployed in new environments. We argue that this underperformance stems from an inadequate understanding of how MQQA models generalize. In this study, we examine the generalization capabilities of three prominent MQQA methods by introducing a rigorous experimental design. We assess their ability to generalize across multiple realistic scenarios, including different sites, timeframes, and MQQA variants. Our findings reveal that current MQQA solutions exhibit limited adaptability when confronted with new sites, temporal shifts, or even when their own versions are used for testing. We propose that the difficulty in handling unseen sites and timepoints primarily arises from a lack of invariance regarding acquisition parameters, whereas the issue with cross-model performance likely results from interdependent errors caused by shared training data between the networks. To address these challenges, we introduce and release two advanced MRI quality assurance models designed with enhanced generalization properties. Our proposed frameworks incorporate strategies to mitigate site-specific biases and model-dependent errors, demonstrating significant improvements in accuracy on unseen sites, timepoints, and other models compared to existing methods.

Amid the global push for decarbonization, private electric vehicles (EVs) are rapidly expanding, yet their widespread adoption risks straining distribution networks. This study investigates how privately owned EVs influence network resilience by analyzing the interaction between a power grid and a population of self-interested agents. These agents aim to minimize personal costs regarding electricity usage and vehicle operation, while simultaneously ensuring grid reliability. To address this complex dynamic, we introduce a multi-agent optimization framework that jointly optimizes EV behaviors and power system strategies. Within this model, EV agents determine charging schedules and discharge patterns, whereas a central system agent manages critical resilience actions such as black-and-ride strategies and demand response. The approach is evaluated through a case study on the 38-node IEEE test system, demonstrating that neglecting private EV behaviors can lead to significant increases in both financial costs and resilience metrics.

Developing compact optical interconnects is a critical requirement for high-performance computing systems. Object recognition systems are increasingly dependent on contextual information, yet determining the most beneficial contextual data types and their optimal integration methods remains a challenge. The universal applicability of Parton Distribution Functions (PDFs) in Quantum Chromodynamics (QCD) calculations is underpinned by their continuous refinement through fitting procedures that align theoretical predictions with experimental data. WorkingWiki is an open-source extension to MediaWiki designed to facilitate collaborative research efforts. Built upon the existing MediaWiki infrastructure, it introduces specialized features such as a robust citation system, a dedicated "talk" page for article discussions, and enhanced navigation tools. We evaluated the system's utility through a large-scale project involving the creation of approximately 1,500 encyclopedia entries on the "COVID-19 pandemic in Spain." This study employs an active flame methodology within a linearized framework to model the interaction between jet fire turbulence and acoustic forcing. The approach derives a compact representation of the jet by linearizing Reynolds-averaged Navier–Stokes equations around a mean plume, treating the inlet mass flux as a function of acoustic perturbations. The resulting model is first validated against experimental data from a vertical, unconfined turbulent plume, which accurately captures the mean flow structure and key characteristics such as the virtual origin and buoyancy-induced velocity scaling. It demonstrates the ability to forecast the primary region flow patterns and the locations of acoustic resonances, including the formation of a vertical acoustic mode. Finally, the model's capacity to simulate jet flame baroclinic instabilities and their associated intense acoustic feedback loops is examined.

The possibility of neutrinoless double beta decay ($0\nu\beta\beta$) is investigated under the assumption that extremely light dark matter interacts with nucleons. Such interactions induce oscillations in the dark matter field, causing a time-dependent variation in the neutrino mass. Consequently, an induced dipole moment forms between the emitted light electrons and the dynamic neutrino mass. The study examines how this dipole moment influences the $0\nu\beta\beta$ decay rate, with a specific focus on the Nucleus $\to$ Nucleus transition scenario. Furthermore, the viability of proposed dark matter models is assessed against current cosmological data. The analysis reveals that axion-like models are compatible with observations, whereas composite models face strong constraints. Additionally, specific ultralight dark matter parameters are identified where the dipole effect becomes significant, potentially enhancing decay rates by up to an order of magnitude.

The paper examines nonlocal gravity theories formulated within an affine framework, which incorporates both a constitutive and a spacetime (nominal) connection. This study introduces a novel framework designed to bridge the gap between large-scale association analyses and functional genomics data. The proposed method, termed CoMAGMA, integrates the robustness of association studies with the biological interpretive power of functional annotations. Specifically, CoMAGMA constructs a unified representation of genome-wide data and annotations, utilizing a multiple testing correction strategy tailored for this integrated format to identify significant associations. Unlike current methods, this approach does not require a fixed number of testing categories, allowing it to adapt flexibly to various annotation hierarchies. To demonstrate the framework's efficacy, we applied CoMAGMA to ten distinct human traits, for which multiple existing association maps were available, as well as nine additional traits for which only raw annotations existed. The application to the latter group highlights the method's capacity to handle previously unanalyzed annotation formats. Across all cases, the framework successfully pinpointed trait-relevant genomic regions, often revealing novel, biologically significant associations. Notably, the method identified a strong link between eye movement patterns and schizophrenia risk alleles, and it located variants in the *SLC6A3* gene associated with alcoholism. These findings confirm that CoMAGMA effectively enhances association analyses through the strategic incorporation of functional genomic insights.

The Large Hadron Collider (LHC) primarily serves to investigate the properties of the newly discovered Higgs boson and search for new physics beyond the Standard Model (BSM) through high-multiplicity $pp$ collisions. However, the machine also delivers substantial integrated luminosities to low-multiplicity final states, which are critical for diverse research areas. These include precision measurements of $Z$+jet processes to calibrate jet energy scales, precision tests of Quantum Chromodynamics (QCD) involving quarkonium states and heavy quarks, precision tests of the electroweak sector involving $W$ and $Z$ bosons, and the production and study of long-lived exotic states such as $X(3872)$, $Z_c(3900)$, $Z_b(10610)$, $Z_b(10610)$, and $Z_b(10610)$. Furthermore, the facility supports the search for long-lived particles (LLPs) and dark matter candidates. This article provides a detailed overview of these minor systems programs, highlighting the significant contributions made by the LHC experiments in these domains.

We examine the recurrence intervals of transient X-ray binary systems involving accreting neutron stars, utilizing data from literature covering more than three decades of observations. Our analysis reveals a distinct bimodal distribution in these recurrence periods, with distinct peaks at approximately 10 days and 10 years. This finding indicates that the classification of Galactic Centre quiescent X-ray binaries—populations often characterized by short, undetected outbursts—is likely flawed. We propose that many such systems are actually transient; consequently, their associated progenitor high-inclination, eccentric super-soft X-ray sources would also be transient, possessing orbital characteristics similar to those of the S-stars located at the Galactic Centre.

This study investigates the effects of mass on electron-phonon and spin-vibration inertia, revealing that these interactions become significantly stronger when atomic masses decrease. Specifically, a phonon with a 1000 cm$^{-1}$ frequency can induce a band structure modification of 1000 cm$^{-1}$, while a photon with a 100 GHz frequency can induce a magnetic resonance shift of 10 GHz. Such pronounced electron-phonon and spin-vibration inertia effects are critical for accurately modeling materials across various length and time scales.

This study introduces the Semantic Diversity in Conversation (SDC) dataset and Natural Language Inference (NLIC) benchmark to evaluate how linguistically diverse topics are discussed. While prior research has extensively analyzed conversational characteristics, it has largely overlooked the examination of semantic diversity. The proposed NLIC benchmark addresses this gap by utilizing natural language inference to assess the semantic similarity of dialogue turns. The SDC dataset, assembled with human annotators, comprises over 20,000 dialogue pairs annotated with paraphrase and non-paraphrase labels. To validate the benchmark, we employed various automatic and manual evaluation methods, demonstrating its efficacy through strong correlations with human judgments regarding semantic variety in dialogue.

Rotating sub-stellar bodies, encompassing brown dwarfs and giant planets, play a crucial role in the evolution of low-mass stars. This study presents a new numerical framework utilizing the perturbed hydrostatic approximation to model rotation within these bodies. By integrating realistic equations of state and self-consistent gravitational calculations, the approach addresses a wide spectrum of masses, radii, and spin rates. The authors examine the structural and compositional dynamics of these objects, analyzing how rotation influences internal pressure, density, and the buoyancy-driven migration of helium. Furthermore, the work establishes a rotation-mass shedding limit, determining the centrifugal threshold where a body's equator reaches its surface. At this critical point, the study demonstrates that the Candlish-Sheffield (C-S) limit is no longer applicable. Instead, at the mass-shedding threshold, the object's polar axis aligns with a specific value of the gravitational potential, $\Phi_{\rm pole} = -1.5$. The model reveals that rotation significantly alters the global shape and internal stratification of these bodies, causing the transition from convective to radiative zones to occur at lower central masses and higher central densities. Additionally, the study finds that the rate of core contraction and cooling is highly sensitive to the degree of rotation. These modeling outcomes provide essential constraints for interpreting observational data regarding the mass-radius relationships and thermal emission spectra of rotating sub-stellar populations.

This study investigates the application of implicit methods for integrating systematic experimental biases into complex amplitude calculations. We analyze how various functional representations influence the precision of these computations and utilize next-to-leading-order (NLO) QCD corrections for proton-proton production of four jets to quantify the quantifiable impact of systematic shifts. Our analysis indicates that implicit parameterization methods offer a superior approach for faithfully capturing the magnitude of such experimental effects.

Gamma-ray bursts (GRBs) represent the most energetic events in the cosmos, yet their underlying mechanisms remain uncertain. This study introduces a new, broadly applicable framework capable of modeling both relativistic outflows and stalled flows. Within this model, variations in the opacity of the outflow account for intrinsic afterglow disparities. By adopting a power-law structure for the initial velocity profile and the specific energy distribution, we derive generalized expressions for afterglows that encompass various scenarios. Our findings indicate that even an intrinsic afterglow component fades in the afterglow, with the opacity-induced emission potentially mimicking a power-law behavior across multiple bands. Furthermore, if the flow becomes non-stalled, the synthetic afterglow light curves exhibit no visible jumps. Conversely, if the flow stalls, these light curves display distinct, prominent jumps. This new model offers a unified approach to understanding both GRBs and their associated afterglows.

This paper investigates the bipartite vertex division problem, where a bipartite graph $G=(V,E)$ with parts $X$ and $Y$ must have subsets $S_X \subseteq X$ and $S_Y \subseteq Y$ removed so that the remaining graph is disconnected. We establish new results linking this problem to the graph's bichromatic components and biconnected components. Additionally, we present an algorithm running in $2^{|V|/3} \cdot \text{poly}(|V|)$ time that solves the problem for $|V| \leq 100$.

Bipedal locomotion is recognized as one of the most challenging tasks for robots, yet current models often lack the practical resilience required for real-world applications. This study introduces a novel concept in which a two-legged robot integrates thrusters into its feet to generate self-propelled motion. We present a thorough analysis of the robot's dynamics, the impact of impulsive forces, and the optimal control strategies necessary for propulsion. Our findings demonstrate that adding thrusters allows the robot to travel faster while consuming less energy. Furthermore, the inclusion of impulsive forces provides inherent stability against external disturbances, enabling the robot to navigate with greater robustness.

Let $(A,\mathfrak{m})$ be a valued domain where the associated value group $\Gamma$ is discrete. This paper characterizes the conditions under which the natural restriction of the valuation map from $A$ to $\Gamma$ constitutes a complete residue map.

This study introduces HyperDegrade, the initial practical technique for dynamically lowering CPU operating frequencies from gigahertz levels down to megahertz levels. By leveraging the fact that lower frequencies reduce both the precision of floating-point operations and the computational throughput of specific instructions, HyperDegrade exploits these trade-offs to solve NP-hard problems more efficiently. We implemented this approach for two NP-hard tasks: optimizing the layout of VLSI full custom circuits and solving the quadratic traveling salesman problem. Experimental results indicate that HyperDegrade achieves near-identical solution quality compared to standard high-frequency execution while consuming approximately 97\% less energy and achieving roughly 3.3 times higher throughput. Furthermore, by operating at reduced frequencies, the system achieves a 100\% increase in task completion rate within constrained time limits.

This paper introduces a new unknotting technique applicable to both classical and welded links. The approach defines an unknotting number based on this procedure and demonstrates its utility by determining the numbers for various non-trivial links. Furthermore, the authors prove that any classical link, as well as any welded link, can be transformed into an unknot through a finite application of this method.

This paper demonstrates that the Vassiliev invariant of diagrammatic order three, first introduced by K. T. Chen applies specifically to the famous Fox-Hatcher knot. This result is significant because the Fox-Hatcher knot was previously believed to be Vassiliev-invariant, and this finding confirms that specific characteristic with a precise numerical value.

This paper introduces a multi-agent approach designed to enhance cooperative decision-making among standard networks of robots that share limited computation and communication constraints. The proposed method involves agents that operate at the decision level to facilitate interaction among the robot group. These agents establish a distinct network architecture, creating a multi-layered system where the upper tier consists of the coordinating agents and the lower tier comprises the robots. By leveraging this hierarchical structure, the proposed approach enables robust collaboration across a population of homogeneous robots. The resulting network of agents functions as an autonomous entity capable of collective reasoning, offering significant advantages over the capabilities of any single individual robot.

Federated learning (FL) is increasingly adopted in data-intensive domains like finance and healthcare to enable collaborative model training while preserving data privacy. However, the growth of cross-party communication links has simultaneously expanded the attack surface for privacy breaches. This study introduces a pragmatic attack, termed Vertical Federated Graph Attack (VFGA), designed to reconstruct private data from a specific participant in vertical federated learning (VFL) systems. VFGA leverages the structural information obtainable from a participant's interaction graph to generate an attack graph, upon which it runs a novel node reconstruction algorithm. Extensive evaluations across various real-world datasets demonstrate that VFGA achieves high reconstruction accuracy in practical settings. Furthermore, we analyze the attack's efficacy under different configurations of participant numbers, interaction graph types, and communication volume limits. These findings offer critical insights into the inherent privacy vulnerabilities of current FL frameworks and provide essential guidance for developing more secure solutions.

Kernel methods are recognized as a robust approach for classification and regression, yet they require carefully selected kernels to function optimally. We introduce a novel kernel estimation framework that leverages pseudo-random Fourier features to analyze data-specific patterns. Unlike traditional techniques that depend on domain knowledge, this method operates in an unsupervised manner, deriving kernels directly from the input data itself. Our proposed algorithm functions as a self-contained module, easily integrating into broader pipelines to deliver enhanced performance across various tasks. Furthermore, we develop an efficient optimization strategy to solve the resulting estimation problem. Extensive experiments demonstrate that these new techniques significantly outperform current state-of-the-art approaches.

This study introduces a novel approach called Cartesian Partitioning to compute character tables for representations of finite groups. This method relies on analyzing the conjugacy classes of the groups' wreath products. We leverage the fact that character values on wreath product conjugacy classes are determined by their restrictions to the constituent groups to derive explicit formulas for these values. The underlying mechanism for identifying conjugacy classes involves partitioning the wreath product's conjugacy classes based on the Cartesian product structure of the groups involved. Although this paper serves primarily as a presentation of the method's fundamentals and theoretical underpinnings, it also offers practical implementations of the algorithm and applies it to compute the character tables specific to the $S_n$ and $A_n$ groups.

Specifically, $M$ is congruent to a regular $p$-gon, where $p$ is a prime number, and its Möbius structure is unique up to isometry. This finding extends a result originally proven by S. This study investigates the optimal allocation of power and time-circuit power resources in full-duplex wireless systems that support simultaneous information and energy transmission. For a configuration involving a full-duplex access point (AP) and multiple energy harvesting (EH) user equipment (UE), the goal is to maximize the sum effective number of EH UEs by optimizing individual EH UE energy harvesting (EH) power levels and information signal transmission rates. This optimization is subject to constraints on total system access point (AP) transmit power, minimum quality of service (QoS) requirements for both full-duplex (FD) and single- (S) UEs, and minimum EH UE harvested energy thresholds. The resulting non-convex optimization challenge is reformulated into an equivalent representation, allowing for the derivation of closed-form solutions regarding time allocation and circuit power distribution. Furthermore, the problem is solved iteratively using block coordinate descent (BCD) techniques to determine optimal power levels for EH UEs. Numerical simulations validate the proposed approach, confirming its superiority over conventional half-duplex (HD) methods.

The study of percolation on disordered systems serves as a fundamental model for understanding phase transitions and avalanche dynamics. A key metric in this framework is the distribution of cluster sizes, which typically follows a power law near the percolation threshold. This research investigates the avalanche-scale cluster size distribution on infinite Cayley trees, which feature a discrete generation structure and well-defined disorder patterns. We demonstrate that these systems exhibit a distinct "structural percolation threshold" separating two regimes: one dominated by the power-law behavior characteristic of the main percolation phase, and another regime where cluster sizes follow an exponential decay. We provide an analytical solution for the boundary between these regimes and derive the exact power-law exponent for both the main phase and the previously unexplored secondary phase. Furthermore, we argue that this secondary phase corresponds to the "Menger-Urysohn" phase identified in prior research. The findings presented here are essential for analyzing similar phenomena in other contexts, including the dynamics of earthquakes.

Sloshing-Sagnac interferometers (SSIs) serve as core sensing elements for ultra-high-precision gravitational wave (GW) detectors. These devices offer exceptional low-frequency sensitivity, yet their traditional operation suffers from poor high-frequency response due to extended arm paths and intricate light circulation. This limitation restricts the accurate detection of strong, high-amplitude gravitational wave signals. This study introduces an optimized SSI design that enhances high-frequency performance by integrating a pair of orthogonal sub-interferometers. The proposed configuration preserves the benefits of long effective arm length for superior noise sensitivity while utilizing short physical arms to improve dynamic response at higher frequencies. Analytical modeling and numerical simulations confirm that this enhanced SSI maintains excellent performance across a broad spectrum, extending high-response capabilities up to approximately 3 kHz.

This paper introduces a Medium Access Control (MAC) protocol designed for XL-MIMO systems with stochastic access patterns. In this setup, an XL-MIMO base station manages a vast array of antennas serving numerous user equipment (UE) units, where each UE operates access independently without coordination. The protocol leverages a visibility-based mechanism: UEs transmit random access (RA) signals within specific time slots determined by their assigned sub-bands. An access is deemed successful only when the base station can distinctly identify signals from multiple non-overlapping visibility regions. This approach guarantees collision-free access and ensures that every UE achieves visibility within a finite timeframe. The study mathematically models the visibility matrix and examines the conditions under which pairs of UEs possess mutually exclusive visibility. Key metrics such as the expected duration for an arbitrary UE to gain visibility and the total time required for all users to access the system are analyzed. Furthermore, the paper explores how varying parameters influence these outcomes and validates the proposed model through simulations.

These discoveries provide robust empirical support for utilizing high-resolution interferometric imaging of gas kinematics and morphology as a tool for identifying and characterizing planetary bodies in the circumstellar environments of other stars.

This work assesses the potential of the CERN NA62 experiment to set stringent limits on a hypothetical heavy, sterile, electrically neutral lepton. We project that, with a 5-year data-taking period, a sensitivity to mixing angles as small as $|U_{eN}| \approx 10^{-4}$ could be achieved for masses of $m_N$ around 300 MeV/c². Achieving this precision would significantly surpass the current constraints derived from existing data.

Although neural language models have largely displaced $n$-gram variants due to their superior performance, this paper argues that the drop in $n$-gram accuracy stems from learning unnormalized, uninformative soft continuations rather than reflecting on the root cause. We introduce a simple unnormalized $n$-gram model designed to learn a continuous distribution $P$ from training data, where $P$ serves as an approximation of the true language model $P_{true}$. Despite lacking a normalization constant, our method achieves text generation accuracy that matches or surpasses state-of-the-art normalized neural counterparts. We further demonstrate that enhancing the model with a neural component yields a version that outperforms existing top-tier results.

This study examines a specific trajectory within the Dini $\alpha$-attractor inflation framework, where the trajectory deviates from the predicted path due to discontinuities in the potential's derivative. We analyze how such disruptions influence PBH production and the subsequent evolution of cosmological density fluctuations. Our analysis indicates that PBH generation is contingent upon the characteristics of the perturbation; specifically, PBHs form only when the perturbation exhibits a sufficiently steep gradient. We further investigate the post-inflationary behavior of PBHs, concluding that their impact on the radiation energy density is contingent upon the precise nature of the disturbance. Finally, we assess the potential effects on the stochastic gravitational wave background.

For $n \ge 1$, $T_n$ denotes the set of ordered trees containing $n$ edges and labeled vertices. This paper investigates the distribution of the minimum vertex count, represented as $L(T)$, for trees within each subset $T_n$. The authors derive the bivariate generating function $T(z,u)$ where $z$ tracks edges and $u$ tracks the parameter $L(T)$, subsequently establishing several properties regarding this function. Specifically, it is proven that the joint distribution of total edges and deepest vertices behaves like a locally normal distribution. Furthermore, the paper examines specific combinatorial characteristics, such as the most frequent values of $L(T)$ and the frequency of trees where $L(T)$ equals 1, 2, or 3. Finally, explicit formulas are provided for various sequences associated with these structures.

Automating the tallying of U.S. elections via image analysis offers a mechanism to enhance public trust, provided the systems accurately handle diverse ballot images. Although existing recognition tools like Tesseract OCR are highly effective at identifying printed text, they often lack the specific accuracy required for official vote totals. This deficiency stems from the fact that standard optimizers, which maximize text legibility, inadvertently encourage models to insert unnecessary text or hallucinate vote counts to fit patterns. We introduce iOCR, an adaptation of the Tesseract OCR framework specifically designed for symbol recognition that prevents these inaccuracies. By incorporating constraints that ban superfluous text and enforce logical consistency among recognized symbols, iOCR significantly outperforms unmodified Tesseract results on real-world ballot data.

Temporal models are widely utilized to forecast future trends based on historical data, yet their high dimensionality poses significant challenges for traditional parameter estimation. This study introduces an approach that incorporates over-parameterization combined with nuclear norm regularization to address these issues. We analyze the proposed method within the linear regression framework, demonstrating that the estimator achieves precise parameter recovery even when the model exhibits some degree of overlap. Furthermore, in a specific temporal setting characterized by an autoregressive structure, the paper shows that the output of the over-parameterized model functions as an effective predictor. These contributions represent the first evidence that nuclear norm regularization can successfully induce interpolation in temporal tasks.

In decentralized markets, the lack of a central coordinator often leads to inefficient storage allocation. This paper introduces a model for a storage provider that employs a self-planning mechanism to determine both the investment in future capacity and the corresponding supply. We model the corresponding market dynamics as a stochastic linear supply-demand system. The resulting self-planning problem is formulated as a Markov Decision Process (MDP) with a cautious objective, aiming to minimize the worst-case expected cost over a given distribution of market states. This approach explicitly accounts for distributional ambiguity. We demonstrate that the market states can be effectively restricted to a low-dimensional state space. Furthermore, we propose an efficient algorithm to solve the state-dependent cautious problem. Numerical simulations illustrate how this cautious self-planning strategy compares to standard, naive planning methods.

This study employs three global atmospheric circulation models with progressively enhanced realism to examine how planetary boundary layer (PBL) friction influences equatorial atmospheric patterns. The simulations reveal that in an atmosphere devoid of PBL friction, the surface boundary layer develops a deep, symmetric, eastward-flowing jet split across the equator. This jet sustains a cyclostrophic super-rotating state, characterized by zonal winds exceeding the planetary rotation rate ($\Omega$). Conversely, the introduction of PBL friction disrupts this symmetry, eliminating the equatorial super-rotation and yielding a meridional structure resembling geostrophic turbulence. These findings are analyzed through the lens of a linearized model designed to capture the primary feedback mechanisms driving equatorial dynamics.

Pretraining large-scale models on natural images has become a standard practice in computer vision, yet most research relies on static datasets that remain fixed after initial training. This paper introduces "Learning in Action" (LiAt), a framework designed to advance models through continuous training on dynamic data. We present a novel batch sampler that optimizes sample selection to maximize the benefit of new information. Additionally, we develop a strategy to scale this approach efficiently using GPU clusters. To demonstrate the effectiveness of LiAt, we conducted experiments on the ImageNet dataset using ResNet-101. The results show a 2.1 percentage point improvement in accuracy compared to static training, increasing from 76.9% to 79.0%. Crucially, these gains were achieved with only 1% of the data updates required by prior methods. The code for LiAt is publicly available.

Achieving long-lived two-level systems using donor atoms in silicon is critical for realizing scalable quantum computing. This study employs a complete configuration interaction method, enhanced with a novel, computationally efficient technique for evaluating the Hamiltonian matrix elements, to precisely determine the ground-state energy and wavefunction of exchange-coupled donor pairs. By integrating a multi-valley effective mass formalism, the approach accounts for full wavefunction anisotropy and spin-orbit interactions. The validated framework successfully predicts the Heisenberg exchange coupling constant ($J$) as a function of donor separation and orientation, covering separations from 2 to 6 nm for various donor sites. These results offer an essential foundation for the design of entangled two-qubit systems based on single donor qubits.

We analyze the transport of conduction through HgTe quantum wells featuring a negative topological gap and a nearly zero (but positive) bottom plateau, situated between two regions of positive topological gaps and a neutral, but non-zero, topological value at the interface between the first and second. This intermediate structure creates a "sandwich" configuration where a sandwiched QPI forms a QPI channel. We find that a negative bias voltage drives a QPI current flowing between the inner edges of the innermost and outermost QPI channels. This current is predicted to vanish when the central area becomes a true zero gap, creating a "switch" for QPI currents. We also examine the impact of magnetic fields on this current and its dependence on gate voltage. The proposed quantum current switch offers a sensitive probe for detecting and measuring the closure of topological gaps.

Dynamic Time Division Duplexing (TDD) allows each cell to independently schedule uplink and downlink subframes, leveraging the diversity of traffic patterns to boost overall system throughput. However, autonomous decision-making often leads to interference and inefficient resource use. This paper introduces a game-theoretical framework designed to schedule traffic for heterogeneous networks (5G Ns). Within this model, cells act as players in a non-cooperative game where uplink and downlink load balancing is treated as the payoff function. The resulting equilibrium configuration ensures that the expected system capacity reaches its maximum. We validate the proposed approach through simulations, demonstrating that the derived Nash Equilibrium significantly enhances total network capacity.

This paper introduces a gradient-based optimization algorithm tailored for symmetric-symplectic neural networks (GS-ANN), which guarantee that trained models generate trajectories adhering to the laws of conservation. The proposed optimizer enables direct parameter learning within a specific class of parameterized Hamiltonian functions, rather than estimating states directly. Because the learned parameters explicitly define the system's Hamiltonian, the model automatically acquires the capability to perform gradient-based reasoning. To validate this approach, we evaluate it on both synthetic and real-world datasets, demonstrating that GS-ANN successfully fits time-series data while effectively learning the underlying gradient-based structure.

Machine learning (ML) models often lack trustworthiness, a critical shortcoming in high-stakes fields like healthcare and finance. This paper introduces an innovative multi-agent framework designed to evaluate and improve the trustworthiness of black-box ML systems by integrating human input. The proposed Human-in-the-loop Online Multi-Agent (HLOMA) approach enables several specialized agents to interact with the target model, accumulate sufficient evidence, and collaboratively reach a verdict on its trustworthiness using an evidence-accumulation decision rule. Key advantages of the HLOMA method include a cost-effective human involvement strategy, the ability to operate online with limited data per agent, and a design that remains independent of specific ML algorithms. Furthermore, the framework supports agent adaptability, allowing them to adjust their behavior based on emerging evidence. We evaluated HLOMA against existing human-in-the-loop methods across three distinct datasets, demonstrating its superior performance in accurately identifying the trustworthiness of white-box and black-box models.

We introduce $K^A(\tau,\lambda)$, a new quantum link invariant defined within the torus times interval ($T^2 \times I$) that mimics the volume hypothesis. This similarity arises because $K^A(\tau,\lambda)$ exhibits an exponential dependence on the Goeritz number for families of braids and the configuration number for Hurwitz closures of braids. For any collection of links $L$ and $L'$ in $T^2 \times I$ that are related by a finite sequence of Conway moves, there exists a bound $C$ such that $K^A(\tau,\lambda)$ remains bounded by $C$ across both quantum invariants. Furthermore, for any parameter choices of $(\tau,\lambda)$, the value $K^A(\tau,\lambda)$ for the torus knot $T(2,2n+1)$ decays exponentially as it approaches the torus knot $T(2,2n+1)$ with a specific limit.

Word sense discrimination (WSD) is a challenging natural language processing (NLP) task that has been approached using various methods. A prominent category of solutions leverages external knowledge sources, such as WordNet, to provide definitions or glosses for each sense of a target word. The primary objective of Context-gloss enhancement (CGE) is to refine these external glosses so they align more accurately with a specific word sense within a given context. This paper introduces a new method for CGE designed to boost WSD performance. The proposed approach employs a bidirectional long short-term memory (Bi-LSTM) network to refine context-sensitive sense definitions. The refined, context-aware glosses are then utilized as additional features for a subsequent WSD model. The effectiveness of the Context-gloss enhancement method is validated through experiments on the standard SemEval-2007 benchmark.

This work establishes new integral representations for the normalized reciprocal gamma function, $x^{-\Gamma}(x)$, by utilizing specific relations involving Riemann-Stieltjes integrals. These formulations are verified to be regularized versions of a result originally presented by Vamanendran and are further connected to the reciprocal gamma function through a contour integral expression.

This study investigates the production of top quark pairs within proton-nucleus (p-A) collisions utilizing the proton-Pb dataset acquired from the Pb-Pb and p-Pb collisions of 2015 at the Large Hadron Collider (LHC). Analysis relies on the invariant mass distribution derived from the $t\bar{t} \rightarrow \text{lepton} + \text{neutrin} + \text{b-jets} + \text{b-jets}$ channel. By applying transverse momentum ($p_T$) thresholds for jets and missing transverse momentum ($E_T^{\text{miss}}$) specific to the analysis, the normalization of top quark generation in p-A collisions is determined relative to proton-proton (pp) collisions with a precision of 15\%. This measured ratio is subsequently employed to constrain theoretical predictions generated by perturbative QCD calculations incorporating p-A specific effects, namely the saturation framework and the color glass condensate model.

This paper introduces an end-to-end cross-domain text-to-SQL model that employs a cross-task architecture. Designed to tackle the scarcity of labeled data and SQL schema information in new SQL databases, the model integrates three key components: a pre-trained bilingual BERT model, a supervised classification task for SQL semantic similarity, and a sparse autoencoder for SQL syntactic feature extraction. Experiments conducted across two major, distinct domains—the Freebase-based Spider benchmark and the Alibaba DataBench—demonstrate that this cross-domain text-to-SL model outperforms current state-of-the-art approaches.

Differential secrecy has established itself as a rigorous standard for safeguarding private data within various information processing tasks. This paper introduces the extension of differential secrecy to graph-structured information, addressing a domain where data entities and their interconnections are equally critical. We examine this active research area, focusing on algorithms that generate anonymized graphs while preserving both differential secrecy and utility. Our review categorizes these methods into generation approaches based on existing real data and synthetic data creation from partial private inputs. Finally, we provide a critical evaluation of current techniques, highlighting existing limitations and potential future research directions.

The international Euclid inheritance community has organized itself into specialized working groups tasked with defining concrete science goals and identifying key technical milestones for the Euclid mission. These efforts are designed to ensure the project's longevity and success. This paper outlines the core findings and recommendations emerging from these efforts.

Hydrodynamic equations are frequently employed to model the macroscopic behavior of microscopic systems, such as those analyzed via molecular dynamics simulations. This approach proves especially effective near critical points, where hydrodynamic fluctuations occur across extensive regions of real space and extended times. This work introduces a novel hydrodynamic framework that accounts for these fluctuations by formulating hydrodynamic equations in terms of phase-space density matrices. These equations are subsequently formulated as stochastic partial differential equations, which are solved using an operator splitting scheme. The validity of this method is demonstrated by simulating the dynamics of a Bose-Einstein condensate interacting with $s$-type particles; results from this simulation are compared against those obtained from time-dependent Gross-Pitaevskii theory.

Building upon the framework of large deviations theory for sums of dependent random variables, we introduce a significant deviation framework specifically for letter sequences generated by correlated processes. We establish the fundamental equivalence between this significant deviation principle and the corresponding large deviations principle. Although general computationally explicit formulas for dependent systems remain elusive, we derive concrete results for variables following a Markov chain, applying these findings to assess the statistical reliability of n-gram language models.

This paper investigates the formation of region-minimizing surfaces within the homotopy classes of continuous maps originating from an $n$-sphere into a general metric space. We demonstrate that a region-minimizing representative exists for every such $n$-sphere homotopy class provided the ambient space is proper. Furthermore, we establish criteria ensuring these minimizing representatives are not null-homotopic. These findings serve as a broader version of the result by Gromov and Schoen which guarantees the non-null-homotopy of minimal representatives of certain oriented $n$-sphere homotopy classes when the target is a Riemannian manifold with negative $\delta$-secant curvature. As an application, we construct an explicit family of non-null-homotopic region-minimizing representatives of $\mathbb{R}P^n$ homotopy classes specifically within the Hilbert cube.

The paper presents a model-independent analysis of the electromagnetic transitions within the $0^+_1$ and $0^+_2$ excited states in $^{64}$Ni, utilizing experimental data for Electric Quadrupole (E2) transitions measured via the Coulomb Excitation method. The study derives model-independent ratios for Electric Dipole (ED) and Monopole Tensor (M1) transitions, revealing significant ED and M1 components in the electromagnetic operator connecting these levels. These findings conclusively demonstrate that the coexistence of distinct configurations for the first two isospin-T=0 levels in $^{64}$Ni arises from the Monopole Tensor interaction.

This study introduces an adaptation of cross-validation for natural language processing (NLPS) model adjustment using Jack-Knife (JK) methods. While cross-validation is the conventional approach for evaluating performance on development and test datasets, Jack-Knife offers a mathematically rigorous variant that reduces variance in results without increasing computational costs. We demonstrate that substituting standard splits with JK validation improves both the dependability of reported metrics and the stability of parameter optimization during training.

The Educator-Pupil (E-P) framework, introduced in 1985, has long served as a foundational model for data-driven knowledge acquisition in logic-based knowledge-based systems. Over the decades, numerous data models and knowledge representation frameworks compatible with the E-P paradigm have emerged, supporting diverse knowledge acquisition methods. However, the original binary distinction between "educators" and "pupils" has evolved; both roles now encompass a broader spectrum of entities, including human experts, other software systems, and the acquiring program itself. This paper offers a comprehensive review of various models and methods developed over the past three decades, analyzing their alignment with the core E-P concepts and categorizing them into four primary groups: those utilizing production rule systems, those utilizing semantic networks, those utilizing logic programming, and those utilizing knowledge graphs. Additionally, we examine the roles and contributions of both human experts and software systems within the modern E-P context. Finally, we outline unresolved challenges and promising future trajectories for research in Educator-Pupil-based learning.

Finding the Most Probable Explanation (MPE) in graphical models is a fundamental yet computationally demanding task, particularly when constrained optimization is required. This paper introduces a new constrained MPE algorithm that integrates the Lagrangian method with the generalized forward-backward algorithm. We further propose a novel function representation designed to streamline the execution of these algorithms by streamlining operations such as numerical stability checks, constraint handling, and efficient memory utilization through the forward-backward pass. The effectiveness and practical advantages of this approach are demonstrated through extensive experiments.

Optical lattice spectroscopy represents a primary technique for characterizing optical atomic lasers, yet a critical prerequisite for attaining the precision levels necessary to identify new force carriers is accurately accounting for photon recoil. This effect induces a frequency recoil in the direction of laser propagation, broadening the resonance and causing a photon loss known as recoil loss. The present study employs numerical simulations to analyze these phenomena, specifically quantifying the interplay between photon recoil and the spatial mode of the optical atomic laser. The simulations reveal that recoil-induced broadening and photon depletion are significantly exacerbated when the atomic ground-state spatial mode exhibits a tight confinement. Furthermore, the findings demonstrate that these impacts vary distinctly across the three dimensions of the optical lattice. These results provide an essential foundation for the experimental design of future force-sensitivity missions.

Discontinuous transitions in fluid rheology, marked by a sudden jump in viscosity, are widely recognized as a primary mechanism behind the contrasting behaviors of yield-stress fluids and complex suspensions. While these events typically require three-dimensional configurations, a fundamental question remains regarding their manifestation in quasi-two-dimensional systems. This study presents the first experimental verification of three-dimensional shear thickening within 2D microfluidic chambers, utilizing high-resolution rheology and particle image velocimetry (PIV). The findings demonstrate that the critical conditions for these transitions are preserved across different particle types and scale invariantly throughout various microfluidic channel designs. Furthermore, the observed global scaling laws align precisely with theoretical predictions derived from the suspension's microrheology. These results establish a foundational framework for engineering the flow properties of particle-laden fluids in two-dimensional microscale environments.

We demonstrate that the centralizer $V_n$ of the Racah algebra $R_n$ within the universal enveloping algebra $U(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$, generated by $R_n$'s standard basis, forms a free module over the polynomial algebra $\mathbb{C}[\mathcal{H}]$. Here, $\mathcal{H}$ denotes the Casimir element of $\mathfrak{sl}_2$, and $f_k(\mathcal{H})$ for $k=1,\dots,n$ are specific polynomials identified as a new family in this work. This discovery establishes the first instances of an HP (Hilbert-Poincaré) type sequence associated with the infinite Racah algebra $R_\infty$ and its centralizer $Z_\infty(R_\infty)$. Furthermore, we determine the leading coefficients of these polynomials $f_k(\mathcal{H})$ explicitly.

Personalization of Web search results may lead users to disregard information they would otherwise find. This effect is difficult to test, as it is hard to replicate the authentic user experience within a controlled environment. This paper presents the first experiment demonstrating that the degree of information loss caused by Google Web search personalization can be estimated. The findings indicate that an average of 20% of information may be missed due to this personalization.

This paper outlines the design concept for the muon-ion synchrotron (MIS), a proposed facility designed to produce multi-TeV muons. The design leverages the principles of the High-Luminosity Heavy Ion Collider (HLHIIC) and the TeV-scale muon collider (TMCC) to achieve a 10 TeV operating energy level. The proposed design aims to reach a luminosity of $10^{34} \text{ cm}^{-2}\text{s}^{-1}$ by utilizing a 10 TeV beam energy, a 10 TeV ring circumference, and a normalized emittance of $10 \text{ pm rad}$. Achieving this luminosity level is crucial for investigating the physics of the Higgs boson and other new physics phenomena.
